title: An ideal multiple factors through a generic coherent inclusion
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $K,G$ be coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, pqf-def-coherent], let $a:K\to G$ be a monomorphism and let $\xi\in X$ be a point at which the induced module-stalk map is bijective [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. There exist a quasi-coherent module $J$ and a monomorphism $\iota:J\to\mathcal O_X$, surjective on the $\xi$-stalk, and a morphism $\psi:JG\to K$ whose composite with $a$ equals the canonical inclusion $JG\to G$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. No integral closed subscheme or sum of ideals is assumed.

source.place: Tag 01YL, third proof paragraph: the annihilating ideal multiple lies in the ideal-sum submodule. Use the annihilator ideal of the coherent cokernel (Tags 05JU and 05JV). Source read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YL.

proof.text: Put Q = cokernel(a) and q = cokernel.π(a). Apply coherent_kernel_cokernel_sum to K, G and a to make Q coherent. Apply isCoherent_iff_isQuasicoherent_and_isFiniteType to Q and G to obtain the quasi-coherence and finite type needed for scheme-theoretic support and affine products.

The cokernel part of module_stalk_exact says that q_ξ is an epimorphism, hence surjective as a module map. For any y in Q_ξ lift y to g in G_ξ, then use the surjectivity component of ha to lift g to k in K_ξ. Functoriality and the cokernel condition give q_ξ(a_ξ(k)) = 0, hence y = 0. Thus the underlying abelian stalk of Q at ξ is subsingleton.

Apply schemeTheoreticSupport to Q and obtain ideal-sheaf data J, with affine ideals Ann(Q(U)) and closed-immersion range equal to the nonsubsingleton-stalk locus of Q. The final clause of quasi_coherent_ideal_zero_set_affine identifies the same range with the locus of nonsurjective ideal stalk inclusions. As Q_ξ is subsingleton, J.toModulesι is surjective at ξ.

Apply ideal_times_quasiCoherent_affine_sections to J and G. Its powers clause for n=1 proves J.toModules quasi-coherent. Its affine product-range clause says that the image of the product inclusion over V is J(V) • G(V). This submodule lies in the kernel of q(V): for r in J(V) = Ann(Q(V)), linearity gives q(V)(r • t) = r • q(V)(t) = 0. For any section on an arbitrary open U, restrict at each point to an affine V contained in U. Naturality of the composite product inclusion followed by q identifies its restriction with the zero section just computed. Sheaf separatedness gives idealModuleProductι J.toModulesι G ≫ q = 0 globally.

Use Mathlib CategoryTheory.Abelian.monoLift a (idealModuleProductι J.toModulesι G) with the established zero composite. This is the kernel universal property of a mono as kernel of its cokernel. Abelian.monoLift_comp gives the required equality ψ ≫ a = idealModuleProductι J.toModulesι G. Return J.toModules with its kernel inclusion, which is mono. Zero cokernels and zero modules require no separate cases.

lean.statement:
theorem coherent_generic_mono_ideal_factor
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    {K G : X.Modules}
    (hK : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace K)
    (hG : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace G)
    (a : K ⟶ G) [Mono a] (ξ : X)
    (ha : Function.Bijective
      ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace ξ).map a).hom) :
    ∃ (J : X.Modules) (ι : J ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf),
      Mono ι ∧ J.IsQuasicoherent ∧
      Function.Surjective
        ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace ξ).map ι).hom ∧
      ∃ (ψ : idealModuleProduct ι G ⟶ K), ψ ≫ a = idealModuleProductι ι G
